question: Do learned latent-world rollouts and delayed-credit spectral engrams improve probabilistic return forecasting when development data are scarce?
information_rule: Every candidate and control receives identical observations, availability timestamps, universe membership, training dates, seeds, tuning opportunities, and protected boundary.

capacity_and_compute_matching.parameter_control: A widened no-world/no-engram backbone is selected on development data to fall within plus or minus 5 percent of full-model trainable parameters.
capacity_and_compute_matching.compute_sensitivity: A separate sensitivity caps control and candidate wall time at the lower observed budget; parameter count, wall time and peak memory are always reported.
capacity_and_compute_matching.broken_cell_rule: A failed or missing baseline cell invalidates the paired comparison and cannot be omitted.

interpretation_rule: Interpreter parameters and gating are learned only on development data and frozen before protected evaluation. No protected outcome can select a latent world, interpreter, seed, threshold, or portfolio objective weight.
engram_rule: An episode is readable only after its outcome availability timestamp. Stored keys and values are detached historical records; current-query gradients cannot rewrite past episodes. A memory claim additionally requires causal RAFT-style and FreshCast-style controls so retrieval freshness or residual alignment cannot masquerade as utility-retention novelty.
statistical_unit: UTC decision date with all contemporaneously eligible assets retained together

statistics.multiplicity: Holm correction across the predeclared mechanism-control family

chronology.split: contiguous expanding-window development followed by validation and one final protected interval
chronology.embargo: at least the maximum target horizon at every boundary

invalidators: portfolio result derived from overlapping or non-realizable returns
freeze_prerequisites: admitted data manifest and validator receipt
actual split dates, row counts, feature schema, horizons and embargo
official WInS universe and rule snapshot if competition claims are in scope
fixed cost schedule, search spaces, cell budget and resource admission
signed configuration, source and protocol hashes

decision_rule.supported: The complete valid primary interval is above 0.01 nats per observation and calibration is not materially degraded.
decision_rule.negative: The complete valid primary interval upper endpoint is at or below zero.
decision_rule.mixed: A predeclared component or regime improves but the primary rule is not met.
decision_rule.inconclusive: The valid interval does not resolve the practical threshold.
